steps.prompt: Finish these three sentences: “Yesterday I…”, “Every day I…”, “Tomorrow I will…”. What happened to the verb each time?
steps.placeholder: Yesterday I… Every day I… Tomorrow I will…

cards.title: Verbs tell time
cards.body: Tense is the time of a verb. The simple past is for actions that are finished: “I walked.” The simple present is for things that happen now, regularly, or are always true: “I walk to school.” “Water boils at 100°C.” The simple future is for things that will happen: “I will walk.”

cards.title: One verb, three times
cards.text:
Past: I played · she played · they played
Present: I play · she plays · they play
Future: I will play · she will play · they will play
cards.note: In the present, he/she/it adds -s: she plays, it rains. The future always uses will + the base verb.

cards.title: Spelling the past
cards.body: Most verbs add -ed: walk → walked. Ending in e: add -d (bake → baked). Consonant + y: change y to -ied (carry → carried). Short verbs ending consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter (stop → stopped, plan → planned). Irregular verbs change in other ways (go → went): that’s lesson 4.

cards.title: Find the time clues
cards.prompt: Tap the four words or phrases that tell you when something happens.
cards.text: Yesterday we missed the bus. Usually my mom drives us, but tomorrow she will be at work. Next week I will ride my bike.

prompts: Which past-tense spelling rule do you need to remember most (-d, -ied, doubling)?
